# Definition of "Targeted Low-Income Child"

According to 42 U.S. Code § 1397jj(b)(1)(C), a targeted low-income child is one who:

"is not found to be eligible for medical assistance under subchapter XIX or, subject to paragraph (5), covered under a group health plan or under health insurance coverage"

This provision establishes that to qualify as a targeted low-income child, the child generally cannot already have coverage through Medicaid (subchapter XIX) or employer-sponsored/private health insurance plans. However, paragraph (5) provides an exception allowing states to waive this requirement for children enrolled in employer plans to provide dental-only supplemental coverage under specific conditions.

## Program Overview

The Children's Health Insurance Program is under Article XXIII-A of the act of May 17, 1921 (P.L.682, No.284), known as The Insurance Company Law of 1921. The program is administered by the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services.

## Eligibility for Uninsured Children

CHIP covers all uninsured children and teens who aren't eligible for or enrolled in Medical Assistance. To qualify, a child or teen must be: under 19 years of age; a U.S. Citizen, U.S. National or Qualified Alien; a resident of Pennsylvania; and uninsured and not eligible for or enrolled in Medical Assistance.

## Coverage and Benefits

The program provides free or subsidized insurance for children in low-income families who are not eligible for Medicaid or not otherwise insured through private or employer-based insurance. CHIP provides free coverage to children from birth through age 18 whose family income exceeds the Medicaid limit, but is no greater than 208% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL).
